title: Economics: microeconomics and macroeconomics
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Use supply and demand, elasticity, costs and market structures to explain prices and firm decisions, then measure the whole economy with GDP, unemployment and inflation, and explain how fiscal policy, money, banks, the Federal Reserve, interest rates and exchange rates affect it, at the level of AP Microeconomics and AP Macroeconomics.

weeks.6: Market failure, externalities and the role of government
weeks.7: Measuring the economy: GDP and growth
weeks.9: Aggregate demand and supply; fiscal policy
weeks.10: Money, banks and the Federal Reserve

blocks.deliverable: Shift supply and demand curves for five news events.
Compute price elasticity from two price-quantity points.
Compare profit under competition and monopoly.
Week 7 midterm; compute real GDP growth and an inflation rate.
Trace a deposit through the money multiplier.
Explain how a stronger dollar affects exports.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Economic briefing: pick a current economic question (for example inflation, a tariff or a rate change), gather three data series from FRED, explain what is happening with the models from this course, and write a two-page briefing with charts and a balanced conclusion.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
